{
  "angles": [
    {
      "local_key": "buyer_research_beyond_reviews",
      "title": "Reviews and buying research answer different questions",
      "content_opportunity": "Explore why praise about a past experience does not necessarily reveal what led a couple to choose a wedding business, and how asking newly booked clients about that decision could inform advertising and landing-page messaging. Anchor the idea in Whitney’s proposed survey workflow, clearly presented as a proposal rather than a delivered service.",
      "strategic_purpose": "WARM",
      "content_type": "thought_shift",
      "strategic_rationale": "This gives owners a meaningful distinction between evidence that describes satisfaction and evidence that can help shape buyer-facing messaging. It also shows WIA thinking beyond campaign metrics toward the reasons people choose a business.",
      "audience": "Wedding-business owners who have customer reviews but want a better understanding of what influences couples’ decisions.",
      "core_perspective": "Reviews can tell a business what clients thought of their experience; asking newly booked clients what influenced their choice can surface a different kind of evidence, potentially useful when shaping ads and landing pages.",
      "tension": "A business may have plenty of positive feedback yet still lack direct information about why buyers selected it.",
      "wia_expertise_in_action": "Whitney distinguishes reviews from research into buying triggers and proposes surveys for newly booked clients, with responses shared for possible use in ad copy and landing pages. Fallon agrees the idea is worth exploring.",
      "service_relevance": "The conversation connects customer research to advertising and landing-page messaging. Survey setup in LeadLock was proposed for Elevate clients, but implementation is not established.",
      "reader_decision": null,
      "evidence_readiness": "supported",
      "research_questions": [],
      "selection_reason": "The distinction is more consequential than a generic reminder to collect feedback: it connects a familiar asset, reviews, to a specific unanswered buyer question and to WIA’s messaging work.",
      "moment_ids": [
        "moment_320404b2bc5d92895b225dda"
      ],
      "source_assertions": [
        "[moment_320404b2bc5d92895b225dda] Whitney said new Elevate clients were asked for market research and that they often shared reviews instead.",
        "[moment_320404b2bc5d92895b225dda] Whitney proposed surveys for newly booked clients, with responses available to inform ad copy and landing pages.",
        "[moment_320404b2bc5d92895b225dda] Whitney said clients would need to tag people or send the survey; the proposed responses would be saved in a spreadsheet visible to the client and WIA.",
        "[moment_320404b2bc5d92895b225dda] Fallon said she thought the survey idea was good."
      ],
      "inference": "Asking about the decision to book may yield information that reviews of the experience do not provide; the exchange does not establish what answers a survey would produce or how they would change marketing.",
      "qualifiers": [
        "The survey and shared-spreadsheet workflow was proposed, not confirmed as implemented or currently offered.",
        "No client participation, response rate, messaging change, or marketing result is reported."
      ],
      "risks": [
        "Speaker identity labels are unverified.",
        "Do not present the proposed LeadLock workflow as a current feature or delivered client service without verification."
      ],
      "quality": {
        "grounding": 4,
        "strategic_fit": 5,
        "distinctiveness": 4,
        "audience_resonance": 4,
        "source_strength": 4,
        "reasons": [
          "The source supports both the distinction and a concrete proposed application.",
          "The treatment turns a familiar practice into a buyer-insight question tied to WIA’s messaging work.",
          "The workflow and its outcomes remain unverified."
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "local_key": "tour_followup_capacity_and_timing",
      "title": "Tour follow-up has to fit both the couple’s timeline and the venue’s capacity",
      "content_opportunity": "Show how a discussion of inquiry-to-tour data changed when the venue explained its real scheduling constraints. The team considered personalized or virtual contact and a targeted video email for tours booked further out, rather than treating missed tours as solely a lead-quality or cadence issue.",
      "strategic_purpose": "WARM",
      "content_type": "behind_the_scenes",
      "strategic_rationale": "This makes collaborative diagnosis visible: funnel data raises a question, client knowledge adds operational context, and the team considers options that may fit both the buyer’s decision timeline and the venue’s capacity.",
      "audience": "Wedding venues and other wedding businesses that book consultations or tours and need follow-up to work within real operating constraints.",
      "core_perspective": "Follow-up recommendations should account for when a couple can engage and what the business can actually accommodate; a later appointment can call for a different kind of connection in the meantime.",
      "tension": "A venue may want to see couples sooner, while staffing, event schedules, and the condition of the space limit tour availability; a long wait may also leave the couple time to consider other options.",
      "wia_expertise_in_action": "Fallon examined inquiry-to-tour and cancellation data and raised the possibility of reviewing nurture language. Whitney asked about tour practices and suggested a personalized virtual connection for some couples. Fallon proposed a supplemental video email for tours booked further out.",
      "service_relevance": "The exchange shows WIA considering how follow-up and messaging relate to the wider path from ad inquiry to a tour. The suggested follow-up changes are not shown as implemented.",
      "reader_decision": null,
      "evidence_readiness": "supported",
      "research_questions": [],
      "selection_reason": "The venue’s scheduling and presentation constraints make this more useful than generic advice to follow up faster. The exchange shows client context changing the options the team considers, without claiming a fix or result.",
      "moment_ids": [
        "moment_86ec3df1112e407a165587c0"
      ],
      "source_assertions": [
        "[moment_86ec3df1112e407a165587c0] Fallon reported an all-time inquiry-to-tour booking conversion rate of about 11% and said cancellations, no-shows, or ghosting were almost 40%.",
        "[moment_86ec3df1112e407a165587c0] Allie said tours booked more than two weeks out could lose momentum, and described limits on Saturday, early-morning, and Sunday tour availability.",
        "[moment_86ec3df1112e407a165587c0] Whitney suggested a personal or virtual connection for some couples booking tours far ahead.",
        "[moment_86ec3df1112e407a165587c0] Fallon suggested a supplemental video email for tours booked further out."
      ],
      "inference": "Matching follow-up to appointment lead time and operational capacity may be a more useful question than assuming one standard tour schedule will suit every inquiry; no effect of the suggestions is established.",
      "qualifiers": [
        "The 11% figure was described as all-time data; the nearly 40% combines cancellations, no-shows, and ghosting.",
        "Allie’s explanation for cancellations was her impression, not a verified cause for each missed tour.",
        "The personalized connection and video email were suggestions; implementation and outcomes are not reported.",
        "The example concerns one venue’s operating constraints and should not be generalized as a universal scheduling pattern."
      ],
      "risks": [
        "The client’s identity and permission to use this meeting publicly are not established.",
        "Avoid implying that the proposed follow-up would prevent cancellations or increase show-up rates."

        "source_strength": 4,

          "The source includes the client’s specific constraints and the team’s distinct proposed responses.",
          "The collaboration illustrates funnel thinking that considers both buyer timing and business capacity.",
          "The reported figures have limited definitions and the ideas have no documented outcomes."
        ]
      }
    },

      "title": "A campaign with clicks but no conversions calls for checking the whole path",
      "content_opportunity": "Use the corporate-event campaign discussion to show a collaborative investigation: Carmen considered the limited click sample and budget, then examined site behavior with Erin; Erin identified account-level ad links and a wedding banner on the corporate page.         "[moment_e0d8f47e45ba342a1efcd623] Erin said the corporate campaign had been running for about a month and had zero conversions.",

        "[moment_e0d8f47e45ba342a1efcd623] Carmen said she was not reaching a conclusion about why people were not converting."

      "inference": "The exchange illustrates why campaign metrics and the destination experience can be investigated together; it does not establish that the identified links or banner caused the absence of conversions.",
      "qualifiers": [
        "The reported zero conversions applied to the corporate campaign during the period described in the meeting.",
        "The click, click-through, cost-per-click, and budget figures are account observations from that discussion, not evidence of profitability.",
        "Carmen’s proposed click threshold was a judgment for this situation, not a validated general rule.",
        "No final diagnosis, completed remediation, or result is reported."

        "The business and meeting participants are identifiable in the source; publication permission is not established.",
        "Do not imply the site links or banner caused zero conversions or present the proposed click threshold as universal guidance."

          "The exchange documents an actual joint investigation and preserves its unresolved diagnosis.",
          "It demonstrates analysis beyond a single ad metric and makes client collaboration visible.",
          "Reported account details require careful privacy and attribution handling."
        ]
      }
    },

Whitney proposed building WIA’s knowledge base from its website, sales pages, investment guide, and FAQs, and questioned whether the widget should book a consultation without human involvement. Giselle was asked to begin the proposed build.",

      "evidence_readiness": "supported",

        "The team distinguished a chat widget from a more involved AI agent; the exchange does not establish current product capabilities or availability.",

      "risks": [

        "reasons": [

          "The pilot and commercial scope remain unresolved."
